item.title: Walking is good for your mental health - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Now that the winter months have passed and the sun is consistently shining, there are so many opportunities to be outside and enjoy the fresh air. One of my favorite ways to enjoy the nice weather has been taking walks outside. Walking has consistently improved my mood, eased my anxieties and provided a fun way to exercise.

item.title: Outstanding Faculty awardee uses teaching to ‘pour life’ on students - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Dr. Ronald Angelo Johnson, associate professor of history, goes beyond simply talking about the past in his classroom. He invites students to participate and discuss through the lens of common humanity.

item.title: SAVE America Act may complicate Election Day voting - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: The Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, which the House passed in February and the Senate has debated since March 17, would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to cast a ballot in federal elections.

item.title: Sports Take: 4 things to watch as spring practice approaches - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Baylor football’s spring practice opens Tuesday. Here are four major storylines to watch for.

item.title: Ignore conflict clickbait: What you need to know about Iran, military drafts - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: If you’re worried about what a draft or what the Iran war might mean for you personally, listen to foreign policy experts, research your eligibility and — above all — stay engaged. Apathy and misinformation kill as bullets and bombs do, without us even setting foot on the battlefield.

item.title: Baylor baseball searches for consistency amid pitching injuries - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Baylor has struggled to find pitching consistency through the first two months of the season, especially following multiple significant injuries.

item.title: What to Do in Waco: April 2-10 - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Easter break is upon us, just in time for some much-needed rejuvenation as the spring semester fatigue begins to set in. If you’re looking for a quaint afternoon outing or a high-energy evening celebration, this list has got you covered.

item.title: Art Center Waco exhibit intertwines eclectic art forms, whimsical imagery - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Art Center Waco’s current exhibit, titled “More is More is More: A Melody of Maximalism,” will be on view until April 25. The exhibit features a variety of media, messages and materials that invite viewers into an eclectic, intimate world of artistry.

item.title: What you need to know about Artemis II - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Four NASA astronauts have set out on a trip around the moon and back. The Artemis II mission occurs just over 50 years after the last moon expedition with the goal of creating a space station where astronauts could stay for an extended period of time.

item.title: The art of being useless - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: When we allow ourselves to be useless, we’re going against the idea that the value of us as living beings is tied to our output, our bank accounts or our GPA. We give our brains a chance to rest, and more importantly, we give our minds a chance to catch up to our bodies. We remind ourselves that we are human beings, not human doings.

item.title: The outrage machine: Why the internet wants you angry - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: The world will not end just because a rapper dislikes cats, and if you are really offended by Timothée Chalamet's comments, support your local opera and ballet.

item.title: Take the gap year — it might change your life - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: Taking a gap year does not mean abandoning your goals. It means strengthening your ability to pursue them. It allows for reflection, growth and, perhaps most importantly, recovery. When you return — whether to school or another path — you do so with clarity rather than exhaustion.

item.title: Bears hunt out Gophers 67-48 in first round of College Basketball Crown - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: The Bears hopped past Minnesota Wednesday evening 67-48 in their opening game of the College Basketball Crown.

item.title: No. 9 Baylor men’s tennis downs Utah 4-1 despite slow start to singles - The Baylor Lariat
item.description: The Bears found themselves with their backs against the wall Thursday night, trailing in the first set across four singles matches. Comebacks from seniors Zsombor Velcz and Luc Koenig ignited the Bears over Utah.
